newsitem.title: CANADA: Avenor shareholders reject Repap merger.
newsitem.headline: Avenor shareholders reject Repap merger.

text.p: Shareholders of Canadian pulp and paper concern Avenor Inc. on Wednesday rejected the company's controversial proposed C$2.6 billion ($1.9 billion) acquisition of Repap Enterprises Inc..
At a special meeting, Avenor shareholders voted 74 percent against the deal, which was pared down from a previous bid.
Repap shareholders approved the deal at a separate meeting.
The rejection came just two days after Montreal-based Avenor rejected a friendly overture by Canadian pulp and paper rival Domtar Inc. to merge with Avenor and Repap.
Avenor Chief Executive Paul Gagne said he was disappointed with shareholders' rejection of the deal and that the company was not pursuing talks with Domtar or Repap "at this time."
Avenor's bid for Repap was cast in doubt earlier this week when Canada's largest pension fund, which holds a 10 percent stake in Avenor, gave the deal a thumbs down.
Quebec's Caisse de depot et placement said it was unhappy with the C$3.2 billion ($2.3 billion) of debt the merged entity would carry.
Montreal-based Avenor earlier this month cut its stock and debt offer to one Avenor share for every eight Repap shares and excluded Repap's British Columbia operations from the deal.
The original bid was one Avenor share for every 4.25 Repap shares, plus the assumption of C$2.4 billion ($1.7 billion) in debt.
Repap said it would pursue its options in light of the Avenor deal rejection.
"We will advise our shareholders of our alternative plans during the course of next week," Repap Chief Executive George Petty said in a statement.
